question: Does the published UBC facade covariate panel reproduce the seasonal detected-carcass associations and transfer to held-out buildings?
source_version_or_hash: Zulian et al. 2023 DOI 10.5751/ACE-02482-180215; Appendix 1 SHA-256 0baba75389249af1dad546868183f956dd38facef64ae35b04ab761e293fd8a7; 8835 rows
hypothesis: Paper-aligned facade predictors and seasonal candidate sets reproduce the published AICc support pattern
method: Strict 57 x 155 panel audit; seasonal binomial-logit GLMM with log survey-hours offset and one composite facade random intercept; AICc and DHARMa
validation_split: Leave-one-building-out: 8 held-out buildings per season; 32 folds total
baseline_or_control: Intercept-only binomial with the same log survey-hours offset
actual_compute: CPU-only GitHub Actions; glmmTMB and DHARMa; no GPU
results_and_uncertainty: Seasonal AICc support matches the paper; latest weighted LOBO Brier is worse than offset-only in all four seasons; log-loss improves only in fall; 17/32 folds improve Brier and 18/32 improve log-loss; summer has 8 positive visits; fold AUC is unstable and often undefined for single-class folds
limitations: 8 buildings and one temperate Pacific campus; detected carcass presence not true collision probability; no detection correction; no glass product or spectra; no Guangdong/BNBU validation
decision: Retain as descriptive paper-aligned external benchmark only; do not use as transferable predictor or risk-ranking model
next_falsifiable_experiment: Run nested leave-one-building-out candidate selection (choose among full/building-only/vegetation-only/null using training buildings only) against the offset-only baseline; then acquire a second independent site with comparable repeated facade surveys and validate calibration and Brier/log-loss before any nonlinear challenger

hypothesis: The De Groot files provide a distinct observation-process/version benchmark rather than a row-identical Zulian outcome panel
method: Checksum/byte verification; grain and key audit; search-efficiency
actual_compute: Source-level validation only; no predictive split
results_and_uncertainty: Compare source totals and common-key records without joining
decision: 8846 collision rows -> 8831 facade-date keys; 152 fatality events; 142 positive visits; 103 persistence trials; 29 search-efficiency trials; 155 scheduled dates; 303 point-count species rows; cross-source 8 mortality and 171 METHOD mismatches
next_falsifiable_experiment: De Groot and Zulian have 139 shared dates and 16 dates unique to each; no row join allowed; trial-level observation process not yet refitted
column13: Keep as separate observation-process benchmark; do not pool outcomes or treat missing keys as zeros
column14: Reproduce GenEst pkm/cpm/estM from original trial and schedule inputs and reconcile original R model selection against AICc tables

question: Does finite-pane path visibility require both bird-to-pane and scene-source-to-pane legs to be unobstructed?
source_version_or_hash: Analytic RectPatch geometry; code PR #23 merged as ff7377b2c954be32d215bc96c7582088e441e77e; synthetic regression fixtures
hypothesis: An opaque blocker on the real source-to-pane segment must suppress both reflected and transmitted candidate rays
method: Analytic segment-plane intersection and finite-rectangle containment; test reflection with virtual image but real-source occlusion; test transmission
validation_split: Deterministic unit tests only; no empirical split
baseline_or_control: Prior one-leg implementation plus unobstructed source-side fixtures
results_and_uncertainty: Two source-side blocker regressions pass alongside finite-pane
decision: rotation and spectral same-pixel tests; 170 tests passed and 1 skipped on pre-merge head
next_falsifiable_experiment: No measured pane geometry or radiance; no foliage volumetric occlusion; no recognition or behavior probability
column13: Correct geometric path-existence gate; do not infer collision probability or BNBU efficacy
column14: Compare predicted pane hit points and source occlusion against measured multi-view scene photographs and surveyed pane coordinates

question: Does training-fold-only seasonal AICc selection improve held-out-building scores over the fixed full GLMM and exposure-only baseline?
source_version_or_hash: Zulian et al. 2023 DOI 10.5751/ACE-02482-180215; Appendix 1 SHA-256 0baba75389249af1dad546868183f956dd38facef64ae35b04ab761e293fd8a7; 8,835 rows
hypothesis: Repeating scaling and candidate selection inside each outer training fold avoids using the held-out building for model choice and may improve transfer robustness
method: Outer leave-one-building-out; within each outer training fold fit full/building-only/vegetation-only/null seasonal binomial GLMM candidates and select by training-fold AICc; score population-level held-out predictions; paired building bootstrap
baseline_or_control: Fixed full GLMM LOBO and exposure-only binomial GLM with identical log survey-hours offset
actual_compute: CPU-only GitHub Actions; R glmmTMB plus 5,000 seeded building-cluster bootstrap draws
results_and_uncertainty: Pending pinned CI results; no performance claim until all folds converge and artifact is inspected
limitations: One temperate-Pacific campus and eight building clusters; detected carcass presence not true collision probability; no façade-level detection correction; no Guangdong/BNBU calibration
decision: Retain as validation experiment only; do not promote a predictor unless it improves appropriate held-out metrics with uncertainty against both controls
next_falsifiable_experiment: Acquire a second independently surveyed subtropical site with explicit zero visits, effort, carcass persistence/searcher detection, measured glazing and non-overlapping vegetation exposures
